children: The U.K. economy maintains momentum despite headwinds, says Thomas Pugh at RSM UK in a note. A further rise in the U.K. purchasing managers' index for August--with the composite index at 52.5--points to the economy growing by 0.2% to 0.3% in the third quarter, he says. This comes in addition to rising consumer and business confidence. "We might have to stop talking about resilience and actually start talking about a reasonable economic performance this year," Pugh says. However, the labor market remains a weak spot, while input and output prices continue to rise. This makes a Bank of England rate hike this year more likely, though a lack of second-round inflation effects mean staying on hold is probably the right move, Pugh says. (don.forbes@wsj.com)
